paragraphs.title: Trust in God and the Longing to Draw Near

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.”
easy.q: Unto whom does the speaker lift up his soul?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “O my God, I trust in thee.”
easy.q: In whom does the speaker trust?

easy.explanation: He asks, “let not mine enemies triumph over me.”
easy.q: Whom does the speaker ask not to triumph over him?

medium.explanation: He says, “let me not be ashamed.”
medium.q: What does the speaker ask would not happen to him because he trusts in God?

answers: They will be defeated by their enemies
medium.explanation: Verse 3 says, “let none that wait on thee be ashamed.”
medium.q: What is said about all those who wait on the LORD?

answers: To act treacherously or do wrong without reason
medium.explanation: Those who “transgress without cause” are contrasted with those who wait on the LORD and are associated with shame.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does it mean to “transgress without cause”?

answers: Those who wait will not be ashamed, but the transgressors will be ashamed
Those who wait will teach, but the transgressors will guide
Those who wait will be poor, but the transgressors will be rich
challenge.explanation: Verse 3 contrasts those who wait on God with those who transgress without cause.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between those who wait on the LORD and those who transgress without cause?

answers: Trust causes him to ask his enemies for help
Trust leads him to ask God to prevent shame and defeat
Trust causes him to stop praying to God
challenge.explanation: Because he trusts in God, he asks not to be ashamed and not to let his enemies triumph.
challenge.q: How does trust in God relate to the speaker's request for deliverance from shame?

answers: From despair to rejection of God
From a personal prayer to a general statement about those who wait on God
challenge.explanation: The speaker begins with a personal appeal and then speaks generally about all who wait on the LORD.
challenge.q: What movement of thought appears in these three verses?

paragraphs.title: A Request for Guidance in the Way of Truth

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “Shew me thy ways, O LORD.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask the LORD to show him?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “Lead me in thy truth.”
easy.q: In what does the speaker ask to be led?

easy.explanation: The LORD teaches sinners in the way and guides the meek in judgment.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD teach according to these verses?

answers: Because God is the God of his salvation
Because he wants to become an enemy
Because he wants to forget the truth
medium.explanation: He says, “for thou art the God of my salvation.”
medium.q: Why does the speaker ask God to teach and lead him?

medium.explanation: Verse 10 says, “All the paths of the LORD are mercy and truth.”
medium.q: What characterizes the paths of the LORD for those who keep His covenant and testimonies?

answers: Those who humbly seek God's way
Those who boast in their strength
medium.explanation: The meek are described as people whom the LORD guides and teaches.
medium.q: What does “the meek” mean in this passage?

answers: Showing God's ways, teaching His paths, and leading in truth
Deliverance from enemies, inheritance, and kingship
challenge.explanation: The speaker asks God to show, teach, lead, and teach him in His truth.
challenge.q: Which sequence of requests appears in verses 4–5?

answers: He teaches sinners in the way and guides the meek in judgment
He removes them from every path
He delivers them to their enemies
challenge.explanation: Verses 8–9 say that the LORD teaches sinners and guides the meek.
challenge.q: How is the LORD's action toward sinners and the meek described?

answers: They are for those who keep His covenant and testimonies
They are only for the speaker's enemies
They appear only in times of trouble
challenge.explanation: Verse 10 connects the LORD's mercy and truth with those who keep His covenant and testimonies.
challenge.q: What condition is connected with the mercy and truth of the LORD's paths?

paragraphs.title: Mercy, Forgiveness, and the Covenant with Those Who Fear God

easy.q: For what does the speaker ask forgiveness?

answers: The man who fears the LORD
easy.explanation: Verse 12 asks, “What man is he that feareth the LORD?” and says that God will teach him.
easy.q: Who will be taught the way that he shall choose?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “Mine eyes are ever toward the LORD.”
easy.q: Toward whom are the speaker's eyes continually directed?

medium.explanation: Verse 6 says, “Remember, O LORD, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses.”
medium.q: What does the speaker ask the LORD to remember when he seeks forgiveness?

answers: He will have no way to follow
The LORD will teach him and his soul will dwell at ease
medium.explanation: The one who fears the LORD is taught God's way, and his soul shall dwell at ease.
medium.q: What is promised to the person who fears the LORD?

answers: A close relationship and the revealing of His covenant
medium.explanation: Verse 14 connects the secret of the LORD with those who fear Him and with His covenant.
medium.q: What does “the secret of the LORD” refer to in this context?

answers: He asks for forgiveness according to God's mercy and goodness, despite his great iniquity
He claims that he has no iniquity
He asks his enemies to forgive him
challenge.explanation: He says, “For thy name's sake, O LORD, pardon mine iniquity; for it is great.” The surrounding verses appeal to God's mercy and goodness.
challenge.q: How are the speaker's request for forgiveness and God's goodness connected?

answers: Those who fear the LORD receive His covenant revealed to them
Those who fear the LORD are removed from the covenant
Those who fear the LORD hide the covenant from others
challenge.explanation: Verse 14 says that the secret of the LORD is with those who fear Him and that He will show them His covenant.
challenge.q: What relationship between fearing the LORD and knowing His covenant is described?

answers: His eyes are continually toward the LORD
He relies on the number of his enemies
He does not know that danger exists
challenge.explanation: Because his eyes are ever toward the LORD, he trusts that the LORD will rescue him from the net.
challenge.q: Why does the speaker trust that the LORD will bring his feet out of the net?

paragraphs.title: Personal Distress and the Plea for Deliverance

easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “I am desolate and afflicted.”
easy.q: How does the speaker describe himself?

easy.explanation: He cries, “O bring thou me out of my distresses.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask God to do concerning his troubles?

answers: They are many and hate him
They will teach him God's way
easy.explanation: Verse 19 says, “Consider mine enemies; for they are many; and they hate me with cruel hatred.”
easy.q: What does the speaker say about his enemies?

medium.explanation: The speaker asks, “O keep my soul, and deliver me.”
medium.q: What requests are joined together in verse 20?

answers: Because he describes his affliction and pain and asks for mercy
medium.explanation: In the midst of describing his affliction and pain, he asks God to forgive all his sins.
medium.q: Why does the speaker ask the LORD to forgive all his sins?

medium.explanation: The word refers to the troubles and pressures from which the speaker asks God to deliver him.
medium.q: What does “my distresses” mean in this passage?

answers: Desolation, affliction, inner troubles, pain, and many enemies
Learning, truth, mercy, and fear alone
challenge.explanation: The verses mention desolation, affliction, enlarged troubles of heart, pain, and many enemies.
challenge.q: Which combination describes the speaker's distress?

answers: Integrity, uprightness, and his hope in the LORD
The claim that he has no sins
challenge.explanation: He says, “Let integrity and uprightness preserve me; for I wait on thee.”
challenge.q: What does the speaker rely on when asking for protection?

answers: He asks not to be ashamed because he puts his trust in God
He asks to be ashamed so that he may repent
He says that shame comes only from his enemies
challenge.explanation: Verse 20 says, “let me not be ashamed; for I put my trust in thee.”
challenge.q: How is the request not to be ashamed connected with trust in God?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for the Redemption of Israel

easy.explanation: The final verse says, “Redeem Israel, O God.”
easy.q: Whom does the speaker ask God to redeem?

easy.explanation: The request is to redeem Israel “out of all his troubles.”
easy.q: From what does the speaker ask God to redeem Israel?

easy.explanation: The speaker addresses God directly: “Redeem Israel, O God.”
easy.q: To whom is the final request addressed?

answers: It changes from a personal request to a request for Israel
It changes from a request for Israel to a request for enemies
It changes from deliverance to a request for wealth
medium.explanation: After praying about his own distress, the speaker asks for redemption for all Israel.
medium.q: How does the focus of the prayer change at the end of the psalm?

medium.explanation: The final verse begins, “Redeem Israel, O God.”
medium.q: What is the main verb in the final request?

answers: To rescue and deliver from trouble
medium.explanation: The request is for God to rescue Israel from all its troubles.
medium.q: What does “redeem” mean in this verse?

answers: Both ask God to rescue from troubles
Only the final verse expresses hope
The final verse cancels the personal requests
challenge.explanation: The speaker first asks for personal deliverance and then asks God to redeem Israel from all its troubles.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the final verse and the earlier requests for deliverance?

answers: The prayer expands from personal distress to national trouble
The speaker stops trusting in God
The speaker prays only for his enemies
challenge.explanation: The ending broadens the prayer from the speaker's own needs to the redemption of Israel.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “I” to “Israel” show about the scope of the prayer?

answers: It emphasizes trust in God and the request for deliverance
It describes the victory of the enemies
challenge.explanation: The psalm repeatedly expresses trust, asks for guidance and mercy, and ends with a plea for redemption.
challenge.q: How does the ending fit the central message of the psalm?
